item.title: The Week the Wheels Came Off the AI Trade
item.description:
P.M. Edition for Nov. 20. Despite Nvidia’s strong earnings and Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO this week, tech stocks had one of their worst weeks in years. Journal markets reporter Hannah Erin Lang discusses why investors have gone cold on the AI trade. Plus, in a press conference today, President Trump, flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, said there will be new penalties on companies that build data centers outside the U.S. We hear from White House reporter Philip Wegmann about ramifications for the 2028 presidential election. And, to help solve New York City’s bathroom crisis, a company called Throne has installed high-tech toilets across the city. Our tech columnist Christopher Mims visited a bunch of them and he tells us what he found. Alex Ossola hosts.


Sign up for the WSJ's free What's News newsletter.

item.title: America’s Biggest Retailers Say Shoppers Keep Spending
item.description:
Bonus Episode for Nov. 20. Few companies have a pulse on the American shopper like Walmart and Target, and both got a boost in the latest quarter from healthy consumer spending—a good sign for the current quarter that contains much of the crucial holiday shopping season. Target’s turnaround is strengthening, while Walmart’s growing e-commerce business is helping offset shrinking sales at its U.S. stores. Both Walmart and Target raised their guidance for the year. Sarah Nassauer covers big retailers for The Wall Street Journal, and took a close look at these earnings.


Pierre Bienaimé hosts this special bonus episode of What's News in Earnings, where we dig into companies’ earnings reports and analyst calls to find out what’s going on under the hood of the American economy.

item.title: U.S. Floats NATO Membership for Ukraine
item.description:
A.M. Edition for Nov. 20. In a series of talks to end the war between Russia and Ukraine, WSJ’s chief European political correspondent Bojan Pancevski says U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have discussed the idea of Kyiv ceding territory it controls to Russia in exchange for NATO membership, something Vladimir Putin and President Trump have previously rejected. Plus, Sean Cairncross is leaving his role coordinating cybersecurity policy, as the Trump administration responds to a wave of cyber threats. And the Senate passes a bipartisan bill aimed at speeding up energy projects, overcoming concerns it would weaken environmental protection laws. Luke Vargas hosts.


Sign up for WSJ’s free What’s News newsletter.

item.title: Anthropic Pulls Off Historic IPO, But AI Doubts Remain
item.description:
P.M. Edition for Nov. 19. Anthropic completed its record-breaking IPO, with shares closing up 17%. WSJ Heard on the Street writer Asa Fitch tells us some of the biggest winners of the day–and why all the buzz around the company wasn’t enough to prevent a broad market selloff. Plus, Jennifer Hiller, who covers the power industry for the Journal, explains how the AI boom’s data centers are expected to push commercial electricity use higher than residential use this year–the first time that’s happened. And we hear from Journal reporter Feliz Solomon on the legal precedent established by the ruling today that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority. Alex Ossola hosts.
